chunks: Al-Ilal: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Isa, from Muhammad al-Barqi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both)
Regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And they said: Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, nor Ya'uq, nor Nasr."

He said: They used to worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then they died. Their people cried out and it weighed heavily on them. Iblis (curse of Allah be upon him) came to them and said: 'Shall I make for you idols in their images, so you look at them and find comfort in them while you worship Allah?' So he made for them idols in their likeness. They used to worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and look at those idols. When winter and the rains came, they brought the idols into their houses. They continued worshipping Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until that generation perished and their children grew up. They said: 'Our fathers used to worship these,' so they began worshipping them instead of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. That is the meaning of the words of Allah, Blessed and Elevated: 'And do not abandon Wadd nor Suwa'.'
ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the idols Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Ahl al-Bayt elucidates the phenomenon of 'gradual shift' (tadarruj) in idolatry, where the veneration of righteous ancestors' statues evolved into independent worship, a process initiated by Iblis as a subtle deception. It highlights the Shia scholarly understanding that idolatry often begins with good intentions but deteriorates into shirk through generational neglect of the original monotheistic intent. This narrative provides the historical context for the specific names mentioned in Surah Nuh, illustrating how memory of the pious became objects of worship themselves.

en.ammaar-muslim: 3. [3/300] al-Ilal: My father from Sa’d from Ibn Isa from Muhammad al-Barqi from Hammad b. Isa from Hariz from Ja’far b. Muhammad عليهما السلام
about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: “They said: do not abandon your gods. Do not abandon Wadd, Suwa’, Yaghuth, Ya’uq and Nasr” [71:23]

- He said: They (the people named in the verse) used to worship Allah Mighty and Majestic then they died. Their people cried out (because of that) and it weighed heavily on them. Iblis - curse of Allah be upon him - came to them and said: ‘I will make idols for you in their image, you will look at them and obtain comfort while continuing to worship Allah’. He made for them idols in their likeness. They used to worship Allah Mighty and Majestic and look upon those idols. When winter and the rains came they transferred the idols inside their houses. They continued worshipping Allah Mighty and Majestic until that generation died out and their sons grew up. They (the second generation) said: ‘Our fathers used to worship these (idols)’ so they began worshipping them instead of Allah Mighty and Majestic. This then is the interpretation of the words of Allah Blessed and Elevated: “Do not abandon Wadd nor Suwa’a …”
